plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their bidding behavior. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid. There's no strategic advantage to shading my bid up or down in this format. I will bid my true value of $34.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win. Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. With no prior history to suggest collusion or unusual behavior, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing auctions you'd profit from winning. With my value at $14, I should bid exactly $14 to maximize expected profit.
